mbmm

mbmm implements the Mechanistic Bayesian Mixture Model (MBMM) framework of Do, McCarthy, and Rogers (2026), A Mechanistic Bayesian Framework for Latent-State Inference in Vaccine and Infection Immunology.

MBMM infers posterior probabilities of latent immunological states, such as productive infection versus non-establishment or transient/abortive detection, or a boost-responsive versus weak/stable antibody phenotype, from sparse longitudinal biomarker trajectories.

The framework embeds an application-specific ordinary differential equation trajectory model inside a Bayesian mixture likelihood evaluated against Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) reference banks. Covariates are linked to latent-state probabilities through a logistic gate for two classes or a multinomial gate for more than two classes.

The package is deliberately domain-agnostic. Users supply the mechanistic trajectory model, ABC prior, observation model, and covariate data. mbmm supplies the shared inferential engine, including:

  • ABC reference-bank construction;
  • marginal reference-bank likelihoods;
  • leave-one-donor-out scoring;
  • logistic and multinomial gate fitting;
  • likelihood-ratio and permutation tests;
  • fitted-threshold estimation and uncertainty summaries;
  • reduced manuscript-style simulation tools.

Installation

You can install the development version of mbmm from GitHub with:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("linhdo154/MBMM")

Getting started

The Introduction to mbmm vignette walks through the main stages of an MBMM analysis: constructing reference banks, scoring subjects, and fitting the covariate-linked gate model using simulated correlate-of-protection data.

The reduced manuscript-style simulation vignette demonstrates how to generate synthetic cohorts and run the pipeline end to end.

The complete package website is available at:

https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/

library(mbmm)

Citation

To obtain the recommended package citation in R, run:

citation("mbmm")

The methodological framework is described in:

Do, L., McCarthy, J., and Rogers, B. (2026).
A Mechanistic Bayesian Framework for Latent-State Inference in Vaccine and Infection Immunology.
